General Rules & Road Procedures.q: Unless otherwise posted, what is the basic speed limit outside a city, town or village on a primary highway?
opts: 100 km/h
90 km/h
110 km/h
80 km/h

General Rules & Road Procedures.q: When backing a passenger vehicle to the left, a driver should:
opts: Look in the inside rear-view mirror and make steering adjustments as necessary
Look over the right shoulder with occasional glances to the front
Look over the left shoulder with occasional glances to the front
Without shoulder checking, use the inside and outside rear-view mirrors to ensure the best view
General Rules & Road Procedures.a: Look over the left shoulder with occasional glances to the front

General Rules & Road Procedures.q: When passing a large truck on a two-way highway, a driver should:
opts: Leave extra room before returning to their lane
Return to their lane when signalled by the truck's headlights
Return to their lane when the truck is no longer visible in any of their rear-view mirrors
Return to their lane once they have cleared the truck's front bumper
General Rules & Road Procedures.a: Leave extra room before returning to their lane

opts: Glancing towards the blind spot in the direction the driver intends to move
Glancing into the left outside mirror
Glancing into both the inside and outside mirrors
Glancing into the right outside mirror
General Rules & Road Procedures.a: Glancing towards the blind spot in the direction the driver intends to move

General Rules & Road Procedures.q: The term "over-driving" your headlights at night means:
opts: The driver cannot see clearly for 1000 metres
The low beam headlights are not set properly
The driver is travelling at a speed which would not permit them to see an object in time to stop
The driver has had the headlights on for too long a time
General Rules & Road Procedures.a: The driver is travelling at a speed which would not permit them to see an object in time to stop

General Rules & Road Procedures.q: Using the 2-second rule to judge a safe following distance when driving:
opts: Is more accurate on rural highways than in urban centres
Is not accurate at speeds greater than 100 km/h
Is accurate at any speed
Is not accurate at speeds lower than 30 km/h

General Rules & Road Procedures.q: When a driver is stopping behind another vehicle in traffic:
opts: Remain a minimum of 10 metres from the vehicle ahead
Allow sufficient space to move into another lane without reversing
Maintain sufficient space as determined by the 2-second rule
Keep back approximately 1 metre from the rear bumper of the vehicle ahead
General Rules & Road Procedures.a: Allow sufficient space to move into another lane without reversing

General Rules & Road Procedures.q: If another vehicle is following too close, what should a driver do?
opts: Slow down gradually and encourage the other vehicle to pass
Press hard on the brake pedal
Increase speed to 10 km/h above the posted speed limit
Activate the four-way flashers
General Rules & Road Procedures.a: Slow down gradually and encourage the other vehicle to pass

General Rules & Road Procedures.q: When recovering from a skid, a driver should:
opts: Accelerate and steer in the opposite direction of the skid
Brake and counter-steer
Steer in the direction the driver wants the front of the vehicle to go
Brake and hold firmly on the steering wheel
General Rules & Road Procedures.a: Steer in the direction the driver wants the front of the vehicle to go

General Rules & Road Procedures.q: The recommended braking procedure to bring a vehicle to a normal, smooth stop is:
opts: Continually increase brake pressure until the wheels lock
Shift the vehicle into neutral and apply steady pressure to the brake pedal until the vehicle comes to a stop
Pump the brake pedal smoothly until the vehicle stops
Apply brake pressure, ease off slightly just before the vehicle stops, then re-apply sufficient pressure to stop
General Rules & Road Procedures.a: Apply brake pressure, ease off slightly just before the vehicle stops, then re-apply sufficient pressure to stop

General Rules & Road Procedures.q: Which statement describes the steps required to reverse in a straight line?
opts: Keep both hands on the steering wheel and constantly use the inside rear-view mirror for guidance
Place the right hand at the top of the steering wheel, look over the left shoulder and use the outside left rear-view mirror
Place the left hand at the top of the steering wheel and look over the right shoulder through the rear window
Place the left hand at the bottom of the steering wheel and use both outside mirrors
General Rules & Road Procedures.a: Place the left hand at the top of the steering wheel and look over the right shoulder through the rear window

General Rules & Road Procedures.q: When travelling in urban areas, drivers should scan the road approximately:
opts: 25 to 30 seconds ahead
12 to 15 seconds ahead
20 to 30 seconds ahead
1 to 6 seconds ahead

General Rules & Road Procedures.q: When approaching the top of a hill on a two-lane highway:
opts: Exceeding the speed limit is permitted!
Flash the headlights to warn oncoming vehicles
Stay to the right portion of the lane
Keep close to the centre line to prevent others from passing
General Rules & Road Procedures.a: Stay to the right portion of the lane

General Rules & Road Procedures.q: According to the Basic Licence Driver's Handbook, most skids are the result of:
opts: Bad brakes
Icy roads
Bad tires
Driver error
The speed you should travel under all driving conditions
The minimum speed permitted on all highways
The maximum speed permitted when conditions are favourable
The maximum speed permitted except when passing
General Rules & Road Procedures.a: The maximum speed permitted when conditions are favourable

General Rules & Road Procedures.q: In reduced visibility due to fog, smoke or snow, use the:
opts: Park lights
Headlights on high beam
Headlights on low beam
Daytime running lights

General Rules & Road Procedures.q: The recommended method for travelling through a curve on a highway is:
opts: Reduce speed before the curve, stay in the lane and gently accelerate after entering the curve
Maintain speed before the curve, brake in the curve, look ahead and accelerate out of the curve
Cover the brake pedal before the curve, counter-steer toward the outside of the lane and accelerate when exiting
Accelerate before the curve, cover the brake pedal in the curve and accelerate after leaving the curve
General Rules & Road Procedures.a: Reduce speed before the curve, stay in the lane and gently accelerate after entering the curve

General Rules & Road Procedures.q: If the vehicle's right tires travel off the paved portion of the roadway:
opts: Apply the brakes and counter-steer to return to the paved portion of the roadway
Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, ease off the gas pedal, and then gradually return to the paved portion of the roadway
Accelerate slightly, then turn the steering wheel sharply to return to the paved portion of the roadway
Move the vehicle completely off the paved portion, then steer back onto the paved portion of the roadway
General Rules & Road Procedures.a: Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, ease off the gas pedal, and then gradually return to the paved portion of the roadway

General Rules & Road Procedures.q: On a two-lane highway, when passing other vehicles travelling in the same direction, a driver:
opts: Should pass on the left when safe
Should pass on the right when safe
Should always travel 30 km/h faster than the vehicle being passed
Should not pull out to pass until they are within 3 metres of the vehicle being passed
General Rules & Road Procedures.a: Should pass on the left when safe

Intersections & Right-of-Way.q: When approaching an intersection and facing a traffic control light that is showing a green right-turn arrow and a red light, a driver:
opts: Must stop and wait for a green light before turning in the direction of the arrow
May go straight through the intersection without stopping
May proceed when safe, without stopping, in the direction of the arrow
May turn left without stopping
Intersections & Right-of-Way.a: May proceed when safe, without stopping, in the direction of the arrow

Intersections & Right-of-Way.q: Which statement best describes the steps for turning right at a red traffic light?
opts: Right turns on a red traffic light are never permitted
Signal and make sure there is no sign prohibiting the turn, stop, look left and right, yield the right-of-way, then proceed
Reduce speed before the turn, look right for cyclists, signal and proceed
Signal and reduce speed before the turn, look left, yield to vehicles and proceed
Intersections & Right-of-Way.a: Signal and make sure there is no sign prohibiting the turn, stop, look left and right, yield the right-of-way, then proceed

Intersections & Right-of-Way.q: A driver attempting to turn left at a steady green traffic light:
opts: Has the right-of-way over oncoming traffic
Must stop before the pedestrian crosswalk line, then proceed
Has the right-of-way over pedestrians
Must not cross the path of an approaching vehicle unless it is safe
Intersections & Right-of-Way.a: Must not cross the path of an approaching vehicle unless it is safe

Intersections & Right-of-Way.q: When turning left from a two-way road onto a one-way road, what lane should the vehicle enter?
opts: The lane immediately to the right of centre
The lane nearest the curb on the left side of the one-way road
The centre lane of the one-way road
The right lane of the one-way road
Intersections & Right-of-Way.a: The lane nearest the curb on the left side of the one-way road

Intersections & Right-of-Way.q: When two vehicles approach an uncontrolled "T" intersection at right angles to each other at approximately the same time:
opts: The vehicle on the left must yield the right-of-way
The vehicle on the left has the right-of-way
The vehicle going straight through always has the right-of-way
Both vehicles must stop
Intersections & Right-of-Way.a: The vehicle on the left must yield the right-of-way

Intersections & Right-of-Way.q: Unless otherwise permitted, what lane must a driver be in to turn left from a one-way road?
opts: The lane to the right of centre
The left lane nearest the left curb
The lane closest to the right curb
The centre lane
Intersections & Right-of-Way.a: The left lane nearest the left curb

Intersections & Right-of-Way.q: When are dual turns permitted at an intersection?
opts: Only when turning from a one-way road onto a one-way road
Only when indicated by pavement markings or traffic control signs
Any time there are at least 2 lanes on the road being entered
Only when the road has 6 or more lanes
Intersections & Right-of-Way.a: Only when indicated by pavement markings or traffic control signs

opts: Has a flashing yellow light for one direction of traffic and a flashing red light for the other direction of traffic
Has traffic signs but no traffic control signal lights
Has no traffic control signal lights or traffic signs
Has Yield signs but no Stop signs
Intersections & Right-of-Way.a: Has no traffic control signal lights or traffic signs

Intersections & Right-of-Way.q: Is a driver allowed to turn right at a red traffic control light?
opts: Yes, but only when a sign permits such a turn
Yes, if the driver reduces speed and there is no traffic or pedestrian in the intersection, and no sign that prohibits such a turn
Yes, if the driver stops and there is no traffic, pedestrian or sign that prohibits such a turn
No, right turns on a red traffic light are never permitted
Intersections & Right-of-Way.a: Yes, if the driver stops and there is no traffic, pedestrian or sign that prohibits such a turn

Intersections & Right-of-Way.q: When encountering a funeral procession that is crossing an intersection:
opts: Sound the horn before proceeding
Proceed through the funeral procession only when there is sufficient space between vehicles
Yield the right-of-way and do not break through the procession
Flash the high beam headlights before proceeding
Intersections & Right-of-Way.a: Yield the right-of-way and do not break through the procession

Traffic Circles, Highway Lanes & Merging.q: A single solid white line between driving lanes in an urban area means:
opts: It is a line separating traffic travelling in opposite directions
Traffic on the right is moving faster than traffic on the left
Lane changing is not permitted
Lane change is permitted

Traffic Circles, Highway Lanes & Merging.q: A "parking lane" as defined in the Basic Licence Driver's Handbook is:
opts: A lane closest to the curb, where parking is permitted but there are no meters
All of these responses are correct
That portion of a primary highway between the edge of the roadway to the right of the direction of traffic and the nearest solid white line, not being the centre line, marked on the roadway
A lane immediately beside a row of parking meters in an urban area
Traffic Circles, Highway Lanes & Merging.a: That portion of a primary highway between the edge of the roadway to the right of the direction of traffic and the nearest solid white line, not being the centre line, marked on the roadway

Traffic Circles, Highway Lanes & Merging.q: A "Weave Zone" is best described as:
opts: A place on a highway where the entrance and exit lanes are close together, and vehicles that are slowing to exit the highway must drive between vehicles that are accelerating to enter the highway
An area on the highway that is used for emergency parking
A place where the highway has a series of curves that require the driver to slow down
A limited access area on a highway where a driver can legally back their vehicle when they miss their exit
Traffic Circles, Highway Lanes & Merging.a: A place on a highway where the entrance and exit lanes are close together, and vehicles that are slowing to exit the highway must drive between vehicles that are accelerating to enter the highway

Traffic Circles, Highway Lanes & Merging.q: A driver entering a traffic circle:
opts: Must yield to traffic on the right
Must yield to vehicles in the traffic circle
Has the right-of-way
Must use the courtesy rule and yield to the vehicle that arrived first
Traffic Circles, Highway Lanes & Merging.a: Must yield to vehicles in the traffic circle

opts: A lane where vehicles reduce speed when exiting a highway
The right lane of a four-lane highway for use by slower moving vehicles
The lane immediately to the right of a solid yellow line on a highway
A lane on hills for use by slower moving vehicles
Traffic Circles, Highway Lanes & Merging.a: A lane where vehicles reduce speed when exiting a highway

opts: A lane with broken line markings
A lane on hills, designated for faster moving vehicles
The left lane of a four-lane highway, for use when passing slow moving vehicles
A lane in a merge area for use by vehicles entering the highway
Traffic Circles, Highway Lanes & Merging.a: A lane in a merge area for use by vehicles entering the highway

Traffic Circles, Highway Lanes & Merging.q: When driving in the right lane on a highway, what should a driver do if another vehicle attempts to merge from an acceleration lane on the right?
opts: Stop to allow the other vehicle in
Accelerate to close any gap in the traffic flow
Move into the left lane if it is safe to do so, or be prepared to adjust speed
Insist that the other vehicle yield the right-of-way
Traffic Circles, Highway Lanes & Merging.a: Move into the left lane if it is safe to do so, or be prepared to adjust speed

Traffic Circles, Highway Lanes & Merging.q: When facing a Merge sign a driver should:
opts: Stop at the entrance to the other highway and wait until a gap in traffic occurs before proceeding
Watch for a gap in traffic on the highway they are entering, adjust to highway speed in the acceleration lane and blend in smoothly
Stop and yield the right-of-way to traffic already on the highway
Reduce speed and proceed with caution
Traffic Circles, Highway Lanes & Merging.a: Watch for a gap in traffic on the highway they are entering, adjust to highway speed in the acceleration lane and blend in smoothly

Traffic Circles, Highway Lanes & Merging.q: When a "PASSING LANE AHEAD" sign is posted, the driver of a slower moving vehicle should:
opts: Use the right lane and reduce their speed to half the posted speed limit
Use the left lane only
Increase speed
Move into the right lane when safe
Traffic Circles, Highway Lanes & Merging.a: Move into the right lane when safe

Traffic Circles, Highway Lanes & Merging.q: A solid yellow line together with a broken yellow line marked on the centre of a highway means:
opts: The road narrows ahead
If the solid line is on your side, passing is permitted
If the broken line is on your side, passing is not permitted
If the broken line is on your side, passing is permitted
Traffic Circles, Highway Lanes & Merging.a: If the broken line is on your side, passing is permitted

Traffic Lights & Control Signals.q: A traffic-lane control light with an illuminated red "X" means:
opts: Prepare for an emergency vehicle travelling in that lane
Reduce speed to below 30 km/h
Use that lane only for the purpose of making left turns
Travel is not permitted in that lane
Traffic Lights & Control Signals.a: Travel is not permitted in that lane

Traffic Lights & Control Signals.q: A driver approaching a flashing red traffic light must:
opts: Stop and wait for the flashing green light
Reduce speed and proceed with caution
Stop and proceed only when safe to do so
Stop until the signal light turns green
Traffic Lights & Control Signals.a: Stop and proceed only when safe to do so

Traffic Lights & Control Signals.q: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
opts: The traffic light will turn green
Stop until the light stops flashing
The traffic light will turn red
Proceed with caution

Traffic Lights & Control Signals.q: When approaching an intersection displaying a steady yellow traffic light:
opts: Proceed since the light is about to turn green
Yield to vehicles on the right
Stop before the intersection unless the stop cannot be made in safety
Increase speed to clear the intersection
Traffic Lights & Control Signals.a: Stop before the intersection unless the stop cannot be made in safety

Special Zones & Restricted Vehicles.q: A "slow-moving vehicle" sign must be displayed on the rear of any vehicle that normally travels at speeds less than:
opts: 50 km/h
40 km/h
70 km/h
60 km/h

Special Zones & Restricted Vehicles.q: The speed limit in a construction zone must be obeyed:
opts: Only during daylight hours
Only when a flag person is posted nearby
At all times
Only when construction workers are present

Special Zones & Restricted Vehicles.q: Unless otherwise posted, the school zone speed limits are in effect on school days during the following hours:
opts: 8:30 A.M. to 1 hour after sunset

Special Zones & Restricted Vehicles.q: When approaching the rear of a stopped school bus that has its alternately flashing red lights activated, a driver must:
opts: Sound the horn to alert any pedestrians and pass at a slow rate of speed
Stop behind the bus and wait until the alternating red lights stop flashing
Move to the left lane, reduce speed to 30 km/h and pass cautiously
Stop behind the bus, look carefully for pedestrians and, if clear, drive past the bus slowly
Special Zones & Restricted Vehicles.a: Stop behind the bus and wait until the alternating red lights stop flashing

opts: From 8:30 A.M. to 1 hour after sunset.
From 8:00 A.M. to 8:00 P.M.
During daylight hours and until 11:00 P.M.
Only when school lets out at noon and after 4:30 P.M.
Special Zones & Restricted Vehicles.a: From 8:30 A.M. to 1 hour after sunset.

Special Zones & Restricted Vehicles.q: When approaching the rear of a school bus that is displaying alternating flashing amber lights, a driver should:
opts: Be prepared to stop as this is a warning that the alternating flashing red lights will come on once the bus has stopped
Be prepared to stop as this could be a warning that there is a collision ahead and the traffic flow has stopped
Stop immediately because the school bus is loading or unloading students
Use caution as the school bus is approaching a railroad crossing and is about to stop
Special Zones & Restricted Vehicles.a: Be prepared to stop as this is a warning that the alternating flashing red lights will come on once the bus has stopped

Special Zones & Restricted Vehicles.q: When approaching a railway crossing that has the flashing red light and bell activated:
opts: Cross the tracks if the train is a minimum of 250 metres away
Reduce speed, check for trains, and then proceed across the tracks
Do not stop and do not change gears while crossing the tracks
Stop at least 5 metres from the nearest rail until the train has passed
Special Zones & Restricted Vehicles.a: Stop at least 5 metres from the nearest rail until the train has passed

Special Zones & Restricted Vehicles.q: Why is it not safe to pass a loaded log-haul truck that is turning?
opts: The driver of the truck needs to fully concentrate on the turn and does not need the added responsibility of a passing vehicle
Loaded log-haul trucks obey the 6-second rule for turns
A danger zone exists as the overhang of the logs from the tail end of the truck could block all the lanes on a highway during the turn
It is illegal to do so
Special Zones & Restricted Vehicles.a: A danger zone exists as the overhang of the logs from the tail end of the truck could block all the lanes on a highway during the turn

Special Zones & Restricted Vehicles.q: At 9:00 A.M. on a school day, what is the maximum speed permitted in a school zone in a rural area, unless otherwise posted?
opts: 50 km/h
20 km/h
40 km/h
30 km/h

Pedestrians & Sharing the Road.q: When approaching a Yield sign, you must:
opts: Yield the right-of-way to traffic not facing the sign and all pedestrians in the intersection
Always sound the horn to warn other traffic within the intersection
Expect all other vehicles to yield the right-of-way to you
Come to a stop and proceed after looking to the right and left
Pedestrians & Sharing the Road.a: Yield the right-of-way to traffic not facing the sign and all pedestrians in the intersection

Pedestrians & Sharing the Road.q: When a vehicle is stopped to allow a pedestrian to cross the road, other vehicles that are approaching from the rear:
opts: May pass the stopped vehicle if there is no oncoming traffic that may impede passing safely
Must not pass the stopped vehicle. It is illegal
May pass the stopped vehicle when eye contact is made with the pedestrian and the pedestrian stops
May pass the stopped vehicle when the pedestrian crossing signal has changed to 'Don't Walk'
Pedestrians & Sharing the Road.a: Must not pass the stopped vehicle. It is illegal

Pedestrians & Sharing the Road.q: In an urban area, when a pedestrian is standing at a crosswalk with their arm raised at approximately right angles to their body and pointing to the opposite curb, what does this mean?
opts: Drivers must stop and yield to the pedestrian
The pedestrian is visually impaired and needs assistance to cross the road
Drivers do not have to yield to the pedestrian until they step off the curb
Drivers should reduce speed to 20 km/h and be cautious when passing the pedestrian
Pedestrians & Sharing the Road.a: Drivers must stop and yield to the pedestrian

Parking Rules & Distances.q: When parallel parking, the vehicle's wheels closest to the curb must be within what maximum distance?
opts: 80 centimetres from the curb
30 centimetres from the curb
10 centimetres from the curb
50 centimetres from the curb

Parking Rules & Distances.q: Which direction should a vehicle's front wheels be turned when parked uphill on a two-way road with a curb?
opts: Parallel to the curb
To the left
To the right
Straight ahead

Parking Rules & Distances.q: Before leaving a parallel parking space on the right side of a road:
opts: Turn on the right signal
Shoulder check to the left
Shoulder check to the right
Use an arm signal straight out and up

Parking Rules & Distances.q: How close can a driver legally park a vehicle to a Stop sign?
opts: 10 metres
5 metres
3 metres
1.5 metres

Parking Rules & Distances.q: Parking in a space reserved for persons with disabilities is permitted:
opts: When all other parking spaces are filled
While the driver is waiting in the vehicle
When a driver stops for less than 5 minutes
When the vehicle has a proper identifying placard or licence plate.
Parking Rules & Distances.a: When the vehicle has a proper identifying placard or licence plate.

Parking Rules & Distances.q: When completing an angle park, the vehicle's front wheel must be within what maximum distance from the nearest curb?
opts: 100 cm
50 cm
25 cm
75 cm

Laws, Demerits & Administrative Rules.q: Alberta has a demerit point system where a fully licenced (non-learner, non-probationary) driver is suspended when they accumulate:
opts: 15 points
8 points
5 points
12 points

Laws, Demerits & Administrative Rules.q: Does a parent have the right to withdraw a previously given "parental consent" for someone under 18 years of age with respect to an operator's licence?
opts: Yes, provided the person is still under the age of 18 and is not self-supporting or married
Yes, provided that both parents verbally agree to withdraw the consent at a registry office
No, once it is given it remains in effect until the person reaches 18 years of age
No, but another consent form must be signed by both parents after a licence suspension
Laws, Demerits & Administrative Rules.a: Yes, provided the person is still under the age of 18 and is not self-supporting or married

Laws, Demerits & Administrative Rules.q: Under the Graduated Driver Licensing program, a driver will receive 2 demerits:
opts: For having more passengers than there are seat belts
For not wearing a seat belt securely fastened
For not wearing a seat belt
For not wearing a seat belt properly adjusted
Laws, Demerits & Administrative Rules.a: For having more passengers than there are seat belts

Laws, Demerits & Administrative Rules.q: According to the law in Alberta, it is the driver's responsibility to ensure that all passengers under what age are properly restrained in the vehicle?
opts: 18 years
24 years
21 years
16 years

Laws, Demerits & Administrative Rules.q: Who is responsible and legally obligated to report any medical condition, change in health, or physical disability that may affect a driver's ability to drive?
opts: The driver's employer
The driver
The driver's doctor
The driver's insurance company

Laws, Demerits & Administrative Rules.q: Under the Graduated Driver Licensing program, what is the minimum amount of time that a person must serve as a probationary Class 5 driver?
opts: 6 months
18 months
2 years
1 year

Laws, Demerits & Administrative Rules.q: A driver is required to report all collisions to the police when persons have been injured or killed, or when combined damage to all vehicles or property is more than:
opts: $2000 (Standardized modern Alberta threshold)

Laws, Demerits & Administrative Rules.q: A road test will be refused by a driver examiner if:
opts: The vehicle has a seating capacity greater than 7
The vehicle is registered as a farm vehicle
The vehicle is a rental vehicle
The vehicle is not mechanically safe
Laws, Demerits & Administrative Rules.a: The vehicle is not mechanically safe

Laws, Demerits & Administrative Rules.q: Is a driver allowed to exceed the speed limit when passing another vehicle?
opts: Only when passing more than one vehicle at a time
Yes, but not more than 10 km/h over the speed limit
Yes, on primary highways only
No, it is never permitted

Laws, Demerits & Administrative Rules.q: In Alberta, the law requires that seat belts must be worn:
opts: Only while carrying passengers
Properly at all times
Only when driving at highway speeds
Only when driving in the city

Laws, Demerits & Administrative Rules.q: Under the Graduated Driver Licensing program, a learner with a Class 7 licence is not permitted to drive a vehicle between the hours of:
opts: Midnight and 5:00 A.M.
Midnight and 7:00 A.M.

Laws, Demerits & Administrative Rules.q: Under the Graduated Driver Licensing program, a learner with a Class 7 operator's license is suspended when they accumulate:
opts: 15 demerits
12 demerits
8 demerits
7 demerits

Laws, Demerits & Administrative Rules.q: When a head restraint is raised to the proper position, the centre of the head restraint is:
opts: Level with the top of the ears
Level with the top of the shoulders
Level with the neck
Level with the top of the head
Laws, Demerits & Administrative Rules.a: Level with the top of the ears

Laws, Demerits & Administrative Rules.q: In the Basic Licence Driver's Handbook, "nighttime" is defined as the period of time:
opts: Beginning 1 hour before sunset and ending 1 hour after the following sunrise
Beginning at sunset and ending at the following sunrise
Between 7:00 P.M. and 7:00 A.M.
Beginning 1 hour after sunset and ending 1 hour before the following sunrise
Laws, Demerits & Administrative Rules.a: Beginning 1 hour after sunset and ending 1 hour before the following sunrise

Laws, Demerits & Administrative Rules.q: A vehicle exiting a parking lot onto a roadway:
opts: Must stop only if there is a Stop sign
Must come to a complete stop
Must stop before crossing the sidewalk only if there are pedestrians present
Is not required to stop
Laws, Demerits & Administrative Rules.a: Must come to a complete stop

Visual Road Signs & Pavement Markings.q: This sign indicates: [White bus icon on green circle]
opts: Route for vehicles over 4500 kg.
Route for slow moving vehicles
Reserved lane for buses
Dangerous goods route

Visual Road Signs & Pavement Markings.q: This sign indicates: [Car shifting over pavement step icon]
opts: Off-road facilities ahead
Slippery when wet
Uneven pavement
Detour ahead

Visual Road Signs & Pavement Markings.q: This sign indicates: [Right bending arrow]
opts: Traffic entering from the right
Winding road ahead
Curve right
Concealed intersection on the right

Visual Road Signs & Pavement Markings.q: This sign indicates: [Yield triangle inside warning diamond with up arrow]
opts: Do not enter
Slow moving vehicles ahead
Warning, Yield sign ahead
Warning, traffic is approaching

Visual Road Signs & Pavement Markings.q: This sign indicates: [Left line narrowing inward]
opts: Road narrows, left
Two-way traffic
Divided highway ends
Obstruction - keep left

Visual Road Signs & Pavement Markings.q: This sign indicates: [Three crests/bumps series icon]
opts: Rumble strips
Construction zone
Bump
Pavement ends

Visual Road Signs & Pavement Markings.q: A large "X" painted on the pavement indicates:
opts: Construction ahead
The traffic lane is ending
Railway crossing ahead
Wild animal crossing ahead

Visual Road Signs & Pavement Markings.q: This sign indicates: [Two cars side-by-side inside red circle with line through it]
opts: Heavy trucks only
Do not pass
No vehicles allowed
Do not enter

Visual Road Signs & Pavement Markings.q: This sign indicates: [Right lane closing inward marker]
opts: Lane ends, loss of right lane
Added lane (free flow)
Curve right
Dual turn lane ahead
Visual Road Signs & Pavement Markings.a: Lane ends, loss of right lane

Visual Road Signs & Pavement Markings.q: This sign indicates: [Pedestrian silhouette walking sign]
opts: Playground zone
Pedestrian crosswalk
Designated school bus stop
School zone

Visual Road Signs & Pavement Markings.q: This sign indicates: [Thick letter 'T' intersection marker]
opts: T intersection
Traffic lane ends
Concealed intersection
Trucks entering highway ahead

Visual Road Signs & Pavement Markings.q: This sign indicates: [Vertical wavy snake-like arrow]
opts: Winding road ahead
Weave zone ahead
Slippery when wet
Lane changing permitted

Visual Road Signs & Pavement Markings.q: This sign indicates: [Branch splitting off right at 45 degrees]
opts: 'T' intersection
Winding road ahead
Merging traffic
Road narrows to the right

Visual Road Signs & Pavement Markings.q: This sign indicates: [Two lanes curving out leftward concurrently]
opts: Through lane only
Passing permitted
No turns permitted
Double lane left turn

Visual Road Signs & Pavement Markings.q: This sign indicates: [Split arrow options to go straight or right]
opts: Sharp left curve in the road ahead
Left turns are prohibited
